html:
Philadelphia is a city in Pennsylvania in the eastern United States, on the Delaware River. It was founded in 1682 by the Quaker William Penn on the land of the Lenape, and its name means "brotherly love" in Greek.

Penn laid it out on a grid and promised freedom of religion. By the 1770s it was one of the largest and richest cities in British North America and the home of Benjamin Franklin, printer, scientist and statesman.

It was the city of American independence:

  • The Continental Congress met there, and the Declaration of Independence was adopted there in July 1776.
  • The Bank of North America, the country's first commercial bank, opened there in 1781.
  • The Constitutional Convention wrote the US Constitution there in 1787.
  • It was the national capital from 1790 to 1800, while George Washington was president for most of that time.

A yellow fever epidemic in 1793 killed about a tenth of its people. It had a large free Black community, where Richard Allen founded the African Methodist Episcopal Church, and it was a stop on the escape routes north. Harriet Tubman fled there in 1849. In the 1800s it became a great industrial city of textiles, locomotives and ships.
sum: Philadelphia is a city in Pennsylvania in the eastern United States, on the Delaware River. It was founded in 1682 by the Quaker William Penn on the land of the Lenape, and its name means "brotherly love" in Greek.
